author: centennial state news
title: Student entrepreneurs showcase businesses at Mesa Mall during annual trade show
text:
The Mesa Mall was transformed into a marketplace of student-owned businesses last weekend as local students participated in the annual Young Entrepreneurs Academy (YEA!) Trade Show on June 10. The event allowed students to present businesses they had spent months developing and preparing to launch.
Throughout the afternoon, shoppers visited booths to learn about various products and services, ask questions, and interact directly with the student entrepreneurs. For participants, the Trade Show marked the culmination of extensive work and growth. Unlike classroom presentations, this event placed students in a real-world environment where they introduced themselves to strangers, explained their offerings, answered questions, and communicated the value of their businesses in real time.
“They learn what it feels like to stand behind something they created themselves and share it with the public,” organizers said. The YEA! program pairs students with local business leaders, mentors, investors, and guest speakers while teaching them how to develop business plans, market ideas, solve problems, and bring concepts to life. Organizers said that along the way students gain confidence, strengthen communication skills, and develop an entrepreneurial mindset that will benefit them beyond the program.
This week marks graduation for this year’s YEA! class as they celebrate completing another successful year. While the Trade Show provides an opportunity for community members to see firsthand what these young entrepreneurs have accomplished, organizers said it also serves as a reminder of each student’s personal growth throughout the program.
Organizers credited local business leaders, volunteers, and community partners for supporting participating students each year. “When communities invest in young people,” organizers said, “the return extends far beyond a single event. It strengthens the future workforce, future business community, and future leadership of Mesa County.”
